validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/OWNER/CLASSIFICATION: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) so wiki_citations.json is empty for this row per the scope note; the sheet's ref set is entirely MISSING_REF, so no existing sheet-cited source could be re-checked either -- this is new research from scratch. Open-web search this run was severely constrained: the session's WebSearch quota was exhausted before I could use it, and DuckDuckGo (html/lite), Bing, Brave, Google, Yahoo, Mojeek, Qwant, Startpage, and Marginalia all failed via WebFetch (CAPTCHA challenges, HTTP 429/403/500, or stale/irrelevant cached results unrelated to the query). One DuckDuckGo html attempt did succeed and surfaced a genuine independent source: Dawn.com (Pakistan's leading English daily, unrelated to GEM), 'SNGPL begins work on 600km gas pipelines' (Ali Hazrat Bacha, 18 Nov 2017), https://www.dawn.com/news/1371244, verified OK via url_verifier.py (200, contains 'Mardan-Swat' and 'SNGPL'). Exact quote: 'With the execution of several mega gas projects including the 111km long Mardan-Swat Gas Transmission Line in progress...' This independently confirms (a) a real SNGPL project literally named 'Mardan-Swat Gas Transmission Line' exists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa -- not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity; (b) owner = Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL), matching the sheet's Owner1; (c) it is explicitly described as a 'Gas Transmission Line', matching PipelineType=transmission (not a gathering/feeder line); (d) Fuel=Gas is trivially confirmed. This is only ONE independent source (tier=medium, not high) despite genuine effort -- a second corroborating source could not be located this run due to the search-engine outage described above, not for lack of trying. Minor naming caveat: the sheet's StartLocation is 'Nowshera' while the pipeline is named 'Mardan-Swat' -- this is a common Pakistani-pipeline naming convention (named for a nearby city/district rather than the literal terminus village) and Nowshera and Mardan are adjacent KP towns on the same corridor, so this is not treated as an attribution error, just noted.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC (length): The only independent source found, Dawn.com (18 Nov 2017), states the 'Mardan-Swat Gas Transmission Line' is '111km long', versus the sheet's LengthKnown=104.89 km -- a ~5.8% discrepancy. This could reflect planned/budgeted length (2017, project 'in progress') vs. final as-built length (sheet updated 2023-07-11), which is a plausible and common construction variance, but per the corroboration standard I cannot silently pass a material disagreement with only one source available, and that one source does not match the sheet's number. I did not find a second source (independent search engines were largely inaccessible this run -- see existence note) to adjudicate which figure is correct, so I am NOT proposing Dawn as a supporting ref for the Length field (it would be an orphan/contradicting ref, not a corroborating one) and am instead flagging this as an open spec question for a follow-up pass once search access is restored, or via direct SNGPL/OGRA State of Industry report lookup.

validity.recommendation: Verify against SNGPL's network/system map that P5486 is a genuinely separate parallel trunk and not the same Nowshera->Swat corridor already recorded as P4179 + P4181 under different names/vintages.
validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE check against roster: P4179 'Nowshera-Mardan-Takht Bhai-Sakhakot Gas Pipeline' (Nowshera->KP, 57.99 km, 8in) and P4181 'Sakhakot-Swat Gas Pipeline' (Sakhakot->KP, 68.06 km, 8in) together form a continuous existing corridor from Nowshera through Mardan/Takht Bhai/Sakhakot to Swat -- the same two endpoints (Nowshera, Swat) that P5486 'Mardan-Swat' (Nowshera->KP, 104.89 km, 12in) also connects. This geographic overlap is a legitimate duplicate/relabel risk worth a human check. Arguing AGAINST a straight duplicate: (1) diameter differs materially (12in for P5486 vs 8in for both P4179 and P4181 -- a genuinely larger pipe, not a relabeling of the same pipe); (2) the Dawn.com 2017 article frames the 'Mardan-Swat Gas Transmission Line' as one of several NEW 'mega gas projects' under construction alongside other new lines (an 80-90km Haripur-Hazara line, a 36km Dara Adamkhel-Peshawar line) intended to extend gas to remote Malakand-division areas (Shangla, Kalam, Dir, Chitral) -- i.e., this reads as new capacity being added to an already-served corridor, not a duplicate entry for pre-existing pipe. I could not fully resolve this without SNGPL's own system map (not accessible this run), so I'm flagging it as a review item rather than asserting duplication, but Baird/the researcher should not assume it's clean without a map check.

validity.researcher_notes: STATUS timing caveat: the only independent evidence found (Dawn.com, 18 Nov 2017) describes the Mardan-Swat Gas Transmission Line as 'in progress' (under construction), not yet operating, at that time. The sheet's LastUpdated=2023-07-11 gives ~5.5 years between that snapshot and the sheet's current Status=operating, which is a plausible completion window for a ~100km trunk line, and I found no evidence contradicting completion. However, I also found no direct/positive confirmation of commissioning or in-service date -- I'm not proposing a ref for Status because Dawn's 2017 text would misrepresent the current claim (it says 'in progress', not 'operating'). This is a soft caveat, not a hard concern: operating is more likely true than false given the elapsed time, but it remains formally unconfirmed by any source I could access this run.

summary: P5486 (Mardan-Swat Gas Pipeline, Nowshera->Swat, KP) is a real SNGPL transmission project, independently confirmed via one Dawn.com (2017) article -- not a GEM-only entity -- but only medium/low tier support was achievable this run due to a session-wide search-engine outage (WebSearch quota exhausted; DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave/Google/Yahoo/Mojeek/Qwant/Startpage/Marginalia all failed). Flagged: a material length discrepancy (104.89 km sheet vs 111 km in the one source found), a corridor-overlap duplicate-risk against P4179+P4181 (mitigated by a differing 12in vs 8in diameter), and an unconfirmed current 'operating' status (source only shows 'in progress' as of 2017).
